issues_detected.description: Institutional attribution is internally inconsistent: data_governance.accountable_organization, the license Licensor and creators[0].id use Washington University in St. Louis (ROR 01yc7t268), while the IRB of record, the reliance contact (hsdrely@uw.edu), the PI's RO-Crate affiliation and the NIH RePORTER awardee are all University of Washington. The record transcribes both and caveats the conflict rather than resolving it; the FAIRhub-side value is very likely a source metadata error
issues_detected.recommendation: Keep the caveat; flag the ROR/affiliation discrepancy to the FAIRhub record owners so the managing-organization metadata can be corrected upstream

issues_detected.description: DOI prefix 10.60775 is not among the rubric's named registrars (PhysioNet 10.13026, Zenodo 10.5281, Dataverse 10.18130); it is consistent with the FAIRhub landing page (fairhub.io/datasets/3), the citation and version_access, and the license DOI 10.5281/zenodo.17555036 uses a known prefix
issues_detected.recommendation: No change needed; plausibility is established by cross-field consistency with the FAIRhub platform rather than by a listed prefix

issues_detected.description: funders[0].grants[1].id and [2].id are fragments minted on the OT2 award's RePORTER URL (#P30DK035816, #UL1TR003096); they resolve to the wrong award. The grant numbers themselves are well-formed NIH identifiers and the minting is caveated
issues_detected.recommendation: Record the P30 and UL1 grants with their own RePORTER project URLs or leave id unset rather than minting fragments on another award

issues_detected.description: download_url is unpopulated; access is documented via page, third_party_sharing and data_governance.access_review_process (https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access), which together give platform access instructions but no direct download endpoint
issues_detected.recommendation: Populate download_url with the FAIRhub access page so the slot the rubric names carries the link

issues_detected.description: software_and_tools is absent. Preprocessing names target standards (OMOP, DICOM, Open mHealth) and describes the pipeline only as 'a mix of automated and custom steps'; no conversion software, versions or repositories are named even though external_resources lists https://github.com/AI-READI
issues_detected.recommendation: Add software_and_tools naming the conversion/curation tools (e.g. .fda/.sdt to DICOM converters, FIT to Open mHealth, OMOP ETL) with versions and the specific AI-READI repositories

issues_detected.description: is_deidentified.method states no active de-identification was applied (FAIRhub 'NoDeIdentification'), while participant_privacy.anonymization_method describes 'removal of protected health information' and the caveat records a Nature Metabolism claim of HIPAA Safe Harbor. The tension is acknowledged and source-ranked in source_caveats, but a reader of the two slots alone sees different claims
issues_detected.recommendation: Harmonize the two slots: state that no direct identifiers were collected, that a HIPAA identifier check was run, and that sex/race/medication were withheld as a disclosure control rather than as de-identification

issues_detected.description: sensitive_elements carries one entry with sensitive_elements_present=false (healthsheet reading) and two with true (RO-Crate categories; controlled-access elements). Both tier-1 readings are represented deliberately, but the list is not machine-interpretable as a single answer
issues_detected.recommendation: Scope each entry explicitly (public release vs controlled-access release) so the boolean values do not contradict each other at the same scope

issues_detected.description: variables lists 17 well-described measures (type, unit, measurement technique) but none carries an identifier or OMOP concept id, and the list covers a small fraction of a dataset whose clinical data are OMOP-mapped across 15+ data types
issues_detected.recommendation: Link variables to the participants.json / OMOP concept identifiers and extend coverage to the imaging, wearable and environmental modalities

issues_detected.description: keywords (7) omit the program and project names (Bridge2AI, AI-READI), 'salutogenesis', 'multimodal' and 'type 2 diabetes' as a phrase; searchability for the program depends on title and description
issues_detected.recommendation: Add Bridge2AI, AI-READI, salutogenesis, multimodal, type 2 diabetes, OCT, wearable sensor

issues_detected.description: No conflicts-of-interest statement accompanies the ethical review documentation; ethical_reviews records IRB approval and bioethicist involvement only
issues_detected.recommendation: Add a competing-interests statement (the BMJ Open protocol carries one) to ethical_reviews

issues_detected.description: instances[0].data_topic B2AI_TOPIC:43 is a syntactically valid CURIE on a declared prefix, but its label is not resolvable from the record itself
issues_detected.recommendation: Carry the topic label alongside the CURIE in notes so the topic is readable without the Bridge2AI standards registry

semantic_insights: All three NIH grant numbers are well-formed: OT2OD032644 (OT2 activity code, OD institute), P30DK035816 (P30, NIDDK), UL1TR003096 (UL1, NCATS), and the primary award is cross-checked against RePORTER application 10471118 with amount, dates and PI

Temporal chain is consistent: IRB approval 2022-12-20 -> collection 2023-07-19 to 2025-05-01 -> version 3.0.0 issued 2025-11-17, within the award period 2022-09-01 to 2025-08-31 plus a no-cost tail; prior releases 2024-05-03 (v1) and 2024-11-08 (v2) are ordered correctly
Cohort counts reconcile: subpopulation totals (race 380+545+519+836; sex 951+1,329; diabetes 776+560+686+258) each sum to 2,280, and split sizes 1,576+352+352 = 2,280

file_collections sizes and counts are internally consistent with the headline totals: nine collections sum to 356,334 files and about 3.816 TB against total_file_count 356,343 and total_size_bytes 3,815,969,779,678 (the residual is the CDS root metadata files)

Ethics block is fully coherent for a human-subjects prospective study: involves_human_subjects=true, IRB STUDY00016228 with reliance agreements, written consent with published form and withdrawal terms, USD 200 compensation, and an honest statement that no DPIA was conducted

De-identification claim (no direct identifiers collected; HIPAA identifier check; sex/race/medications withheld) is appropriate to the data type and consistent with confidentiality_level 'restricted', the disease-specific-research permission and the watermarking/re-identification prohibitions in the license

Source conflicts (publisher, institution, enrolment start, de-identification framing, sensitive elements, sampling, target enrolment, license openness, year labelling) are enumerated with a declared ranking rather than silently resolved
Bias entries use BiasTypeEnum values (selection_bias, sampling_bias, representation_bias) each paired with a mitigation strategy grounded in the wave-based recruitment design

Per-modality standards are consistent across conforms_to_standard, distribution_formats and file_collections (DICOM for imaging, WFDB for ECG, OMOP CDM for clinical CSVs, Open mHealth for CGM and wearables, ESDS for environmental, CDS for directory structure)
The web banner 'under review for potential modification in compliance with Administration directives' is correctly placed in notes rather than in status
